# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 16
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 16

---

*[The brightness of the righteous. The commission. Peter's tabernacle proposal.]*

1. We, the twelve disciples, beheld him as though he had been taken up into the heavens, and the brightness of the light in him did not cease.

2. I saw all the righteous who were there with him. They shone with a brightness ten times greater than the sun, and their whiteness was whiter than any snow.

3. The joy of those who dwelt in paradise was great. They praised the Lord greatly, together with all the angels who praised him.

4. The Lord asked us: "Do you behold the glory that is here? Do you see those who are with me? And what will be the end of this vision?"

5. We answered him: "We do not understand. For before we could speak, our understanding was taken from us."

6. The Lord said to me: "Go and tell all those who are to enter my kingdom in the manner of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. To all of these shall be given the crown of faith."

7. I said to him: "Lord, will you permit me to speak two words — that you may understand what I am about to say?"

8. He said to me: "Speak what you wish, my Lord."

9. I said: "A great light has appeared before us today — a light more beautiful than any light we have known. If it is possible, let us make three tabernacles — one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah."

10. He said to me: "You see the kingdom of heaven in advance, Peter."

---
*LOGOS note: "Two words" (v.7) is a Semitic idiom for "a few words" — not a literal count. The Lord's response to Peter ("Speak what you wish, my Lord") addresses Peter as "my Lord" — a remarkable inversion that may reflect the intimacy of the visionary relationship, or a textual peculiarity.*
